R2
enablers: EN01 · Validate the core tutoring workflow and establish measurement baselines
Exploration
R1
Resolve the highest-risk assumptions before treating the proposed slices as a delivery commitment.
Produce a test plan for learner teacher-choice/booking intent and teacher brief→lesson→recap tasks, including teachers who prefer minimal/printable tools.
Record task completion, preparation effort, errors and qualitative evidence without pooling inconsistent interview denominators.
Publish findings, baseline definitions and a continue/change/stop recommendation; separate observed results from hypotheses.
Research synthesis and interactive simulations exist; new validation results and success thresholds are not established.
EN02 · Define safeguarding, guardian authority and data-handling policies
Policy / exploration
R1
Make the unresolved safety and privacy decisions that production account, identity and meeting flows depend on.
Create a reviewed decision register for eligibility, guardian authority/consent, reporting/escalation, blocking and safe in-person meetings.
Define public/private fields, identity-provider data boundaries, retention/export/deletion and explicit recording/transcription consent; recording remains off by default.
Link each decision to affected stories and record unresolved launch gates; identity checks must not be represented as proof of teaching quality or guaranteed safety.
Policies remain open; identity/guardian previews do not record real consent or establish legal compliance.
EN03 · Define commercial rules and evaluate payment/payout providers
Policy / exploration
R1; extends to R2 payouts
Give booking, cancellation and earnings flows an explicit commercial contract and provider boundary.
Document price/fee display, cancellation/refund/no-show handling, teacher compensation and dispute responsibilities for review.
Evaluate payment/payout provider capabilities, failure states, callbacks and reconciliation in a sandbox; record the selection rationale and open questions.
Define payout eligibility, fees, timing and initiation policy before R2 money movement; no placeholder price or cancellation window becomes policy.
No real provider or commercial policy is agreed; this issue enables decisions and sandbox evidence, not real financial transactions.
EN04 · Establish shared domain, persistence and authorization foundations
Architecture
R1
Provide durable, role-scoped state behind the current web/mobile simulations.
Document entities and lifecycle transitions for learner/guardian/teacher, goals, lessons/versions, sessions, messages, recaps and submissions.
Implement a versioned storage/API boundary with server-side ownership/role checks, migrations and isolated synthetic fixtures.
Demonstrate a saved draft surviving refresh and authorized retrieval, cross-account access rejection, immutable completed-session snapshots and consistency across web/mobile clients.
Current state is React memory and resets on reload; backend/storage choice remains open.
EN05 · Integrate production account, guardian and identity handoffs
Technical integration
R1
Replace sample account and identity paths with explicit authenticated/provider states once policy is agreed.
Choose and document authentication/session recovery and identity handoff contracts; keep identity status distinct from qualifications and profile publication.
Implement provider success, pending, failure, deferral and return routing without leaking legal identity into public profile or client logs.
Verify learner/adult/guardian/teacher branches and stale-provider-state clearing using sandbox accounts; guardian authority must follow EN02 decisions.
Email, Google and Persona/document flows are local simulations. Provider selection is not predetermined.
EN06 · Build private material storage and permission-safe sharing
Technical infrastructure
R1
Support real learning resources and deliberate sharing without exposing private drafts or notes.
Define accepted file types, size limits, ownership, retention, safe preview/download and processing safeguards before uploads use real storage.
Implement authorized upload/replacement/removal and recipient-scoped access with observable pending/failed/success states.
Test cross-account access denial, failed upload/send recovery, private-note exclusion, revoked access and preservation of reusable originals.
Local object URLs and sample materials exist; a production storage/delivery service is not connected.
EN07 · Implement consistent scheduling and booking/payment orchestration
Architecture / technical integration
R1
Make concurrent booking and provider retries safe and keep both participants aligned.
Specify a session/payment state machine and time-zone/DST model with conflict checks and atomic slot reservation.
Implement idempotent booking/payment commands, provider callback handling and reconciliation for pending, confirmed, failed and canceled outcomes using sandbox services.
Verify concurrent requests produce at most one confirmed reservation/charge, retry does not duplicate effects, and replacement acceptance preserves the original booking until success.
Teacher booking conflicts and replacement acceptance are local simulations; production terms/provider behavior depend on EN03.
EN08 · Establish messaging, reminders and one-to-one video delivery
Technical integration
R1
Supply the delivery channels needed for confirmed sessions, communication and teacher-approved follow-up.
Evaluate/select channel and video boundaries without automatic recording; document purpose-specific permissions and session membership checks.
Implement durable message/reminder/recap delivery states, safe retry, recipient scoping and notification preferences.
Exercise undelivered messages, duplicate callbacks, camera/microphone denial and call disconnect/rejoin; manually prepared materials remain accessible when optional services fail.
Conversations, lobby and teaching are fictional local flows. No real messaging, notifications or video provider is connected.
EN09 · Set up delivery environments, monitoring and recovery procedures
Infrastructure
R1
Make production changes deployable, diagnosable and recoverable with explicit evidence.
Document environment separation, configuration/secrets ownership, migration/deployment checks and rollback paths; preserve protected mobile runtime boundaries.
Add redacted diagnostics and actionable monitoring for critical booking/share/provider failures; define proposed SLO/RTO/RPO after business/dependency review.
Demonstrate restore/reconciliation and outage handling in an isolated environment, plus a measured representative load/performance baseline.
A frontend build/deployment workflow exists; production backend monitoring, backups, restore and capacity evidence do not. Numeric service targets remain proposals.
EN10 · Establish accessibility, compatibility and end-to-end verification gates
Quality infrastructure
R1
Turn the quality requirements into repeatable evidence across the shared learner/teacher journey.
Define a supported browser/device/input/time-zone matrix and representative learner, guardian and teacher scenarios using synthetic data.

Add meaningful checks for keyboard/screen-reader paths, zoom/reduced motion, private-note exclusion, approval/share, booking conflicts and failed-send recovery; preserve existing runtime integrity checks.
Run the core brief→chosen teacher→booking→approved lesson→session→recap path and publish results/known gaps; proposed accessibility and performance targets require measured evidence.
Existing dated local tests and phone previews are partial evidence, not an accessibility certification, physical-device audit or production-flow verification.
EN11 · Evaluate and integrate optional AI with teacher review controls
Exploration / technical integration
R3
Establish whether real AI assistance improves preparation while retaining teacher responsibility.
Define permitted data inputs, provider boundary and a representative evaluation set for factual accuracy, level appropriateness, practical relevance and harmful/inappropriate output.
Implement labeled draft generation with edit/apply/discard, teacher approval and a tested manual fallback for timeout or unusable output.
Compare preparation effort and correction burden with manual work; record a release recommendation and prohibit unapproved sharing/final evaluation.
Current AI produces labeled sample content only. Advanced AI remains optional and outside the core R1 dependency chain.
EN12 · Implement optional calendar synchronization and conflict recovery
Technical integration
R3
Support optional calendar connections without making manual availability depend on a provider.
Select/document provider permissions, busy/free data minimization, sync direction and source-of-truth rules.
Implement connection/disconnection, incremental sync, duplicate-event handling and date-specific time-zone/DST conversion.
Test revoked access, stale data and provider outages; show sync state, preserve confirmed bookings and retain manual scheduling.
External calendar integration is proposed; Google/Outlook are ideas rather than selected providers.
EN13 · Implement payout ledger, provider handoff and reconciliation
Architecture / technical integration
R2
Provide trustworthy teacher earnings and payout state after the commercial rules are agreed.
Implement a session-to-earnings ledger with agreed fee/refund adjustments, eligibility rules and traceable gross/net amounts.
Integrate payout setup/status with scoped provider access, idempotent transfer requests and callback reconciliation using sandbox funds only.
Verify pending status cannot trigger a second transfer and failed/reversed outcomes preserve an actionable audit trail without leaking financial details.
Payouts are conceptual previews; provider, fees, timing and initiation policy remain open until EN03 is resolved.

nfrData: NFR01 · Accessibility and assistive technology
All learner/teacher flows, web and phone preview

Proposed acceptance: target WCAG 2.2 AA. Every core flow is keyboard operable with visible focus, programmatic names/status/errors, non-colour-only selection and logical reading order. Support text zoom and reduced motion; touch controls remain usable.
Audit automated findings plus manual keyboard, screen-reader, 200% zoom and reduced-motion scenarios across setup, editor, calendar, dialogs and failure paths.
Current interface needs measured audit; no conformance claim. Must be validated before production R1.
NFR02 · Usability and manageable setup

Users can complete one meaningful action per setup screen, go Back without losing answers, skip optional steps and recover from errors with an actionable next step. Teacher lesson preparation remains short/modular and does not require long-form authoring.
Run representative learner, guardian and teacher tasks. Record completion, time, errors and preparation effort versus current methods; establish targets after baseline research.
Prototype behavior exists; user testing and quantitative thresholds are not established. Proposed R1 gate.
NFR03 · Performance and interaction responsiveness
Web/mobile setup, workspace and content

Starting targets for review: usable core screen within 3 seconds on an agreed mid-range mobile/network test profile; visible control response within 100 ms excluding provider completion. Large optional media/AI must not block navigation or manual editing.

Define device, network and p95 measurement window before testing; measure load/interaction traces with representative resources and long lesson/calendar data. Track regressions against the recorded baseline.
Targets are proposals, not measured results or commitments. Prototype/local and deployed production performance are separate.
NFR04 · Browser, viewport and time-zone compatibility

Core tasks remain usable on agreed current Safari/Chrome/Firefox/Edge and representative iOS/Android viewports, keyboard-open states and text zoom. No clipped primary actions or unintended horizontal overflow. Scheduling handles agreed time zones and daylight-saving changes.
Publish support matrix and run representative physical-device/browser tasks including narrow layouts, orientation, long content, keyboard dismissal and DST transition booking.
Phone previews are browser simulations, not native binaries. Current availability supports Europe/Paris only; physical-device and wider zone coverage need validation.
NFR05 · Reliability, durable drafts and transaction integrity
F04–F07, F08 payouts

Acknowledged saved drafts survive refresh/network failure in production. Unsent work never appears shared. Concurrent slot requests and repeated retries create at most one confirmed booking, charge, message or payout. Reusable originals and completed-session snapshots remain intact.

Fault-injection tests for offline/reconnect/refresh, duplicate callbacks, concurrent bookings and interrupted sends. Verify durable state, idempotency and preserved originals; reconcile provider outcomes.
Current state is in memory and resets on reload. Local simulations are not evidence of durable recovery. Production R1 gate before booking/payment.
NFR06 · Privacy, data minimization and consent
F01, F05–F08; all private data

Public profile excludes legal identity, private notes and confidential learning data. Only intended recipients see shared materials. Collect only purpose-relevant information; request permissions in context. Recording/transcription is off by default. Retention, export/deletion and guardian authority require explicit decisions.

Inspect field/recipient matrix, learner previews and data flows; test private-note exclusion and consent/permission states. Review proposed retention and minor-data handling before any real collection.
No legal-compliance certification is asserted. Prototype uses fictional/sample flows; production data policy is open.
NFR07 · Security and role-based access control
Production accounts, messages, lessons, bookings, identity and payouts

Authenticate before private access; authorize learner/teacher/guardian roles server-side for every private operation. Protect data in transit/storage using supported platform controls; keep secrets and identity data out of client bundles/logs; reject cross-account object access.
Threat-model production data paths; test unauthenticated/cross-role/cross-account access, session recovery and secret/log exposure. Resolve material findings before real private data or money flows.
No backend or production authentication exists today. Provider choice, account recovery and guardian permissions remain open; this is a proposed R1 gate.
NFR08 · Availability, provider failure and recovery
Production booking, sharing, video and payment dependencies

Core manual preparation remains available when optional AI/calendar providers fail. Show actionable degraded/pending states; retry safely without false success. Define monitoring, recovery objectives and backup/restore rules before release.
Exercise provider outage/timeouts and restore drills; verify draft integrity and status reconciliation. Set SLO, RTO and RPO after dependency design and business review.
99.9% availability is an optional starting proposal only, not an SLA or current capability. No production service/backup exists.
NFR09 · Transparency and human control
F01–F08, especially AI/identity/sharing

Clearly distinguish simulations from real operations and draft/pending/approved/shared/failed states. Teacher can edit/discard AI and controls final evaluation/publication. Learner explicitly chooses teacher; users confirm recipients and meaningful commitments.
Inspect all success, pending, failure and AI-unavailable paths. Verify no automatic matching, unapproved sharing, hidden recording or claim that identity checks establish teaching quality.
Current prototype labels and manual fallback are source evidence, not a full audit. Proposed R1 gate; real AI-specific verification accompanies R3.
NFR10 · Maintainability, observability and capacity
Shared web/mobile domain and future services

Keep shared domain rules consistent across web/mobile and providers. Protect runtime boundaries; cover guardian branching, visibility, conflicts, snapshots and retries with meaningful regression tests. Production diagnostics use redacted identifiers and reveal actionable failures without private content.

Run relevant existing checks for each change; trace a booking→approved lesson→recap scenario and failure paths. Establish expected usage/load envelope, then load-test against the agreed SLO; capacity is not assumed from sample fixtures.
No scale target is agreed and no production load test exists. Current local tests/build records are dated evidence; future service gates require fresh validation.
